title: Slow-Cooker Vegetable Soup
subtitle: Chunky mixed vegetable soup in the slow cooker
excerpt: Carrots, celery, leek, potato, and tinned tomatoes in a well-seasoned vegetable stock. Six hours in the slow cooker makes a deeply flavoured, chunky soup that needs nothing more than bread to serve.

recipe.sourceNotes: Vegetable soup is one of the most practical uses of a slow cooker. The long, low heat extracts flavour from roots and aromatics that a quick stovetop version cannot match. This is a simple working version using everyday vegetables. The potatoes thicken the broth slightly as they cook. Any root vegetables can be substituted.

content.text: All the vegetables go in raw at the start. Cut them in similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly. The potato breaks down slightly to thicken the broth. If you prefer a thicker soup, mash or blend a quarter of the soup before serving and stir it back in.
Put all the vegetables, garlic, tinned tomatoes, bay leaves, and thyme into the slow cooker. Pour over the stock. Season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Cook on LOW for 6 to 8 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours, until all the vegetables are completely tender.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme stalks. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve in deep bowls with chopped parsley and crusty bread.
